messages:
alex: Swarming — ACME POC seeing intermittent connect timeouts and 'deadline exceeded' on long streaming requests when clients are behind their corporate HTTP proxy. @mira can you take point?

acme_poc_admin: Error snippets: 'Error: socket hang up', 'RequestError: connect ECONNRESET' on Node; Python shows 'socket.timeout: The read operation timed out' and occasional 407 from proxy. Proxy: proxy.corp:8080 with TLS interception. More common at stream start and on long prompts.

mira: Which SDKs and config? Are you using HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env or a proxy wrapper? Any minimal repro?

acme_poc_admin: Node/TS: @redwood/js 1.4.2, Python: redwood-client 0.9.7. Env: HTTP_PROXY=http://proxy.corp:8080. No NO_PROXY except localhost. Node repro:
```
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.KEY, timeout: 120000 });
await client.generate({ model: 'gpt-large', prompt: 'long prompt...', stream: true });
```
Python repro:
```
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate', json=payload, timeout=(5,60), proxies={'http':'http://proxy.corp:8080','https':'http://proxy.corp:8080'})
```
Failures intermittent — sometimes stream starts then dies after a few seconds.

ivan: Likely causes: 1) proxy terminating idle or not handling HTTP/1.1 chunked streaming, 2) TLS MITM adding latency so socket deadlines too short, 3) proxies mishandling 'Expect: 100-continue'.

ivan: Quick mitigations to try:
Node: enable keepAlive and set longer agent timeouts.
Python: increase socket read timeout, use a session with larger pool, enable retries for connection errors.
Also try removing 'Expect: 100-continue' if present.

danielle: Ask ACME infra to check proxy logs for intermittent 407 or CONNECT timeouts — that often explains the behavior.

salesops-bot: POC snapshot: hosted=true; dedicated=false; quotas: 60 rps, burst=120; account_id=poc-ACME-77.

mira: Can you run 2 quick diagnostics and paste output? 1) curl through proxy: `curl -v --proxy http://proxy.corp:8080 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health` 2) openssl s_client: `openssl s_client -connect proxy.corp:8080 -proxy api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai`. Also capture NODE_DEBUG=request,net logs and full Python traceback.

acme_poc_admin: Ran curl, trimmed output:
"*   Trying proxy.corp:8080...
* Connected to proxy.corp (10.1.1.2) port 8080 (#0)
> CONNECT api.redwood.ai:443 HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
* TLS handshake with API failed: EOF
* Closing connection 0"
So CONNECT sometimes succeeds but TLS handshake fails immediately after.

ivan: That matches intermittent TLS interception failures. Next steps: 1) I'll open a PR to default-enable keep-alive when HTTP_PROXY is detected and bump streaming timeouts, 2) add an optional streaming-start retry wrapper for transient ECONNRESET/EOF, 3) provide a short repro/test script for ACME. ETA ~4h for Node PR, follow-up for Python.

mira: :thumbsup: I'll coordinate and ask ACME to run the diagnostics and attach proxy logs. Schedule a screenshare tomorrow if persists.

alex: Please summarise action items for AE.

mira: Summary: - Ivan: PRs to enable keep-alive + increase stream timeout defaults + streaming-start retry (ETA 4h). - ACME: run curl+openssl diagnostics and upload proxy logs; capture NODE_DEBUG and Python tracebacks. - Danielle: validate proxy auth/407 spikes with ACME infra. - Mira: follow up in 4h and schedule screenshare if needed.

acme_poc_admin: Will run diagnostics and upload logs. Thanks for quick triage.
